messages.content: Alonsa awakens to find herself in the same place she fell asleep in last night. Thromb is alseep on the other bed, uncovered by the provided sheets.
“Mm…”
“Oh, I’m… I’m here.”
“Good. Great!”
She hops out of bed
Her words cause Thromb to stir, and his eyes flutter open shortly thereafter. He's quite the light sleeper. "Right. What are your plans today?"
She opens up her backpack and pulls out a large notepad.
“I’d love to get some detailed notes on the church.”
“Oh, but I do need to scout the town out more.”
“And I might have agreed to do something for the bartender? Don’t know how pressing that is
Hopefully also she can put her mind away from… all of that.
He stands up, and equips his winter coat. "The bartender's game is tomorrow. Never a good idea to miss it, but that leaves today open. I can help you find anything in town."
“Hm… I want to scout out whoever is running the train operations.”
"As far as I know, they're working out of a station a short walk from the town. I should be able to take you there, but getting you in could prove difficult."
“hm… maybe later then. When we have a better excuse to go”
“Let’s go to the church.”
He nods, and exits the room.
She changes and follows
Briar is currently speaking with a man in similar police attire as Cory, while the old innkeeper watches from the desk.
Briar wakes up in her one-bed room in the Narita Inn. Light has begun to trickle in through the window's curtains, casting the sun's gaze upon her.
She stretches her arms upwards and yawns. With her eyes still half closed she gets out of bed.
Briar has escaped the clutches of her mattress.
After changing back to her usual clothes, she opens the door to her room and goes towards the entrance of the inn.
The old man is still at the desk, and is currently engaged in conversation with a man in similar attire as Cory. The badge affixed to his outfit labels him as the deputy.
With a smile she approaches them, waiting for their conversation to end to speak.

"Didn't see nothin'. Just showed up out of the blue this mornin'. Real eerie, gotta be a warning o' some kind, huh?" The innkeeper gives a testimony to the deputy.

"I'm not at liberty to discuss any details. Thank you for your assistance." The deputy turns his eyes to Briar. "Hello, ma'am, I have a few questions, if you wouldn't mind."
"Oh hello sir, I don't mind at all!"
"Right. Tell me your name and occupation, for the record, and then I'd like to know where you've been since last night."
"I'm Briar McGregor and I'm a violinist! Hmm... Well, I got here last night with Cory, after that I bought a room and then I slept for a long time. Did something happened?" she looks at him confused

"There's... a situation. The boss has a theory, but I'm not sure I buy it. Just checking alibis of everyone we have placed around here." As the deputy explains this, Alonsa and Thromb make their way down to the lobby.
“Heya!”
Briar waves at Alonsa with a smile but it disappears as she switches to wave at Thromb.

Thromb doesn't return the wave. "More lawmen? Here to harass us?"

The policeman, whose badge labels him as the deputy, shakes his head. "No, that'll be the boss. I'm just getting the facts."
“What’s the occasion?”

"That's confident-"

"There's a body. Came across it this mornin'. Real ugly sight." The innkeeper cuts off the deputy's attempt to conceal information.
Briar gasps looking back and forth and the innkeeper and the deputy
“A body?!”
“Has it been identified?”
The deputy tries to swallow his annoyance. "Not... conclusively. It's in a rough shape. As far as we can tell, no one's gone missing, so it's probably someone from out of town."
“That’s awful…”
"Is there anything identifiable about the body? Anything at all? Height? Hair color?" Briar asks nervously

He thinks over his response, before sighing. "I hate to ask this, but... it could be a real help if you two took a look. We're getting an unusual amount of out-of-towners this week. Could have some connection to you folk, you never know."
“Oh… of course!”
“I took a mortuary science class once. We’ll see if I remember any of it.”
"I- I can try looking"

"What about me? I'm not leaving my client's side unless requested." Thromb questions the lawman.

"Oh, you were gonna hafta come with me anyhow. The boss has his suspicions about you. Seems unfair to me, but whaddaya I know." The deputy leads the way out of the inn.
“I wouldn’t go without you anyway.”
"Right." Thromb nods and follows the deputy.
Briar follows after them
Alonsa does too

Two changes in the town immediately jump out to Briar and Alonsa. The first is a short distance from the inn. In the spot where a golden statue was visible yesterday, there is now a tarp covering the art piece. A small gathering of residents is crowding around the hidden statue, which Cory is currently attempting to placate.

Shortly after taking in that sight, they would notice the looming presence over the town. The stone structure positioned on one end of the town has expanded in size, in a primarily vertical direction. It now stands at three times, or perhaps slightly more, its height the previous day. The stone tower, a quaint church yesterday, is now a visible landmark even from the center of town.
“Huh…”
“What happened?”
“The church expanded?!?”
"...What?" The deputy stares at her in confusion.
“It wasn’t that tall yesterday…”
"What is happening...?" Briar whispered under her breath

"I think I'd notice that. You probably had a long trip, could've just been a mirage yesterday." The deputy dismisses her claims.

Thromb looks uncomfortable, but doesn't say anything.
“You… you see that, right?”
To Briar
"I see it... it wasn't like that last time" she stares at the church confused until she opens her eyes open wide "The bartender! She said something about the church yesterday remember?"
“Mm…”
“We can ask her later…”
“Him, too.”

"Yeah, worst case scenario, you folk noticed some construction I missed. Not nearly as high priority as a body showin' up in the middle of town outta nowhere." The deputy continues towards the crowd, and waves to Cory.
Alonsa follows
Briar follows walking faster

Cory narrows his eyes upon seeing them approach. "Well, I reckon missy here is quite the sight for sore eyes. Cruor over here, on the other hand..." He motions to Thromb. "Now how did I know somethin' like this was gonna happen. Trouble always blows into town alongside you, don't it?"
"Cory, are you okay?" Briar asks looking him up and down

"A damn body shows up in the town square, and you expect me to-!" He stops himself, holding his head in frustration. "Sorry, sorry... Just, wanted to spend my week havin' a nice time out with a little lady... Not investigatin' no murder..."
“Hey, what’s that supposed to mean!”
“Thromb has been with me since days ago.”

"Oh? I'm assumin' if you're vouchin' for his alibi, you've been watchin' him that whole time? Didn't sleep at all last night. Didn't, oh let's say, let 'im walk outta the tavern on his own and catch up with 'im later?"
“I don’t appreciate this. There’s no reason to believe that about him versus anyone else.”
"It's okay, I'm sorry for asking you have a lot on your plate... let's not point fingers right now" Briar sighs, hugging herself "Can I see the body...? I just to make sure it isn't someone I know"
Cory clicks his tongue. "Right. No finger pointin', then. I'll stick to the facts. Fact is, body ain't a pretty sight. Never is, but this one... hoo boy. Y'all sure you can stomach it?"
"I- I will try my best"
“Yes.”

"Right. Good 'nuff for me. The body was found on this gaudy statue. We didn't want to disturb it, so I had my boys go ahead and cover the whole thing. Tryin' not to get the townsfolk restless, y'know. 'Spose word got out anyhow, so no point in keepin' it..." He grabs the base of the tarp in his hand, but just as he's about to gently pull it off, his eyes focus on something in the distance.

The crowd follows his gaze towards a hill overlooking the town square. Just on the outskirts of town, what appears to be a small army has gathered. Alonsa, an expert in Turtima's cultures, recognizes their garb. Briar shares this familiarity, but from personal experience. The Yondovan royal guard has arrived, and they're marching straight towards the crime scene.
((End session))
"Aw bell, don't we got enough problems already?" Cory mutters to himself.
Alonsa remains focused on the body, and attempts to identify it
This is difficult due to Cory only having grabbed the tarp and not pulled it off.
Briar moves closer to Cory while staring at the royal guard
((Oh wait I misread nvm))
“Those are Yondovan royal guards… what are they doing here? Isn’t this being done through private companies?”
"Can't say I know too much 'bout the details, but those thugs came into town a few months back. Oversaw that statue bein' put up." Cory responds.
“Figures…”

The Yondovan guards descend the hill and weave through the town, converging upon the covered statue, and essentially encircling the group who was already here. Three women dressed like civilians arrive alongside the group.
It's early when Atie wakes up. Everyone else in the crew quarters is still asleep, or at least pretending to be, and light's only just begun trickling in.
Atie just stares upward for a bit, having no reason and little energy to get up.
It sounds like there's some commotion in the next car over, but she can't hear exactly what's happening. Penny begins to stir at the noise.
Atie turns and tries to hear what is being said.

It's hard to get the full picture, but she can catch that the Yondovans are being gathered for some reason. Before she can hear much else, the door to the cabin is slammed open. Theo stands in the open doorway panting, face paler than usual and sweat dripping. "There's... problems."
Atie looks at him silently, in shock.

The others seem to have woken up from the slamming. Rhea sits up as if her body is held together by a hinge, while Val casually rolls over to stare at Theo in confusion. Penny looks to be barely keeping herself from hiding under her covers.

Theo catches his breath before continuing with a grave expression. "The Yondovan guard is... heading into town... and I can't find the Emperor anywhere. They're up to something. We *need* to keep an eye on them."
"What? Are they coming for us?"

He groans in frustration. "The situation's... complicated. You don't get a project like this funded without some tension. The specifics would go over your head, just... I need some extra pairs of eyes."
Atie is taken aback. "You won't take ours!"

"I have some in storage." Rhea contributes this, while Val just lets out a hearty laugh.

Theo moves to face palm, but winces in pain from his recently un-dislocated arm. "I need you. To use. Your eyes. And tell me what they see. Because I can only be in one place at a time." His tone is that of speaking to a toddler.
"I don't understand. Aren't yours working?"

"For the Princess's sake..." He mumbles under his breath, then turns to Penny. "Welsh, get Alcule up to speed, and keep an eye on her too. Doma and Van Halen can hold the fort here." He leaves without confirmation.

Penny whimpers out. "I-it was... a metaphor..."

Atie is confused. "Sure, I'm just confused about what he wants us to do with them. Does he mean somewhere outside? Or are we defending the train?"
Before Penny answers, Atie continues. 
"Wait, he just left us behind for you to teach me about the metaphor?"
"W-we're supposed to, um, we're, uh... w-well, I guess we watch the Yondovans? And... report back, to him?" She stumbles out of bed, untangling herself from her sheets.

"Oh! Right! He's worried the Yondovans here are evil!"
Atie gets up and leaves.
Penny follows. The two of them find a gathering of Yondovans in the lounge car. Bucky, Ace, and Bixbite are among a group of royal guards standing at attention.

A banging noise forces Mari awake; the worker on the floor stirring to as well. The sound is accompanied with a voice from outside the door of her room. "U-up and at 'em, maggot!" It's soft and familiar, but putting on an ill-fitting air of strength.
I yawn serenely, stretching my arms out over my head and lifting my feet up. Who's calling me a maggot, exactly? Do I need to be worried?

The worker takes the initiative, and opportunity to get off of the floor, to open the door to the hall. On the other side of the doorway stands Ace, currently dressed up in the attire of a royal guard, looking slightly embarrassed.
Hahaha- what? Oh, wow. This is incredible. This is... a once in a lifetime sight.
I leap to my feet, pulling into a sharp salute and putting on the gravest expression I can manage with how desperate I am to smile. "Reporting, sir!"
His face turns a deep shade of red. "Mmgmgmhhjgh... At ease... Bixbite... *C-captain* Bixbite is gathering a group to head into town, and... wanted me to wake you..."

I finally break at him turning into a tomato. "I- You- AAHAHAHAHAHAHA!! Oh my god Ace what is this. What are you doing. This is fucking. Unbelievable." I run up to him and pull him into a headlock before I start noogieing him.
"S-stoooop, aaawwahgghh..." His arms flail uselessly. "I-it's not... by choice! Bixbite cornered me!!!"
I keep it going for a few more seconds before letting him go, still laughing. "Ace... you look so spiffyyyyy..." I get up in his face and grin at him. "You're a sharp lad, Mr. Acilis, sir!"
I poke him on the cheek before backing away. "Why would Bixbite rope you into this? Did you do something to piss her off? PLEASE tell me you got her worked up about something."

"Sh-she said she enjoyed throwing me around yesterday... So she gets to do that more as my direct superior..." He covers his face.

"Uh. Did she need anything from me, or can I go back to sleep? This whole conversation is pretty awkward to be in the same room as." The other worker says words.

"Oh, shut up. You can leave if you don't like us being friendly." I'm honestly just happy that Ace is doing okay after last night. I don't care if this guy thinks we're awkward. I look back to him. "I guess I can understand that. You're pretty fun to throw around." I smirk goofily.
"Wait, so... does this get you any special privileges? Exclusive access to the barracks or something? Where are you patrolling?"
The worker shrugs and leaves. Once he's gone, Ace responds. "U-um... I get to wear this outfit, I guess... So far my job has literally just been waking you up..."
"Huh. Unfortunate. Well, mission accomplished, soldier!"
I salute again, more loosely this time.
I don't have any specific responsibilities today, correct?
Construction of the railway cannot resume until the political situation is dealt with, so all workers are currently off-duty.
Okay. Alright. I sigh, suddenly anxious. This is the big day, huh? The day I've been waiting for. Nothing holding me back, no excuses. I came here with a goal in mind, and I'm not abandoning it.
"Hey, Ace... do you know *why* Bixbite wanted me awake? She's not looking for me, right?"
"Sh-she is, yeah... Uh, half the guard is heading into town, and... Well, she also wanted you... for some reason?" He appears confused at his own words.
Well, I did say no excuses. "Could you go back and tell her that I'm feeling ill? Like, violently, contagiously ill." I make a gagging sound to sell it.
"I'm not... a very good liar... um..."
"Oh, I'm not lying." I scratch my nose. "Never mind, though. She probably wouldn't care. Fine! I'm coming. Let's just make it quick."
He hesitantly nods, and begins leading the way towards the lounge car. "W-we can find a... doctor in town, probably..."
"No need. You probably already have it, anyways. It's too late for any of us." I say this deadpan, following him to the car.

The two find a gathering of royal guards with Bixbite at the center, who nods in Ace's direction. "Good work Acilis. That's everyone. Let's begin briefing."

As the guards stand to attention, two of the train's crew emerge behind Bucky and Ace. Atie and Penny enter the lounge car.
Bixbite ignores the new entrants to the lounge, while Ace gives them a subtle wave. Penny looks ready to explode.

I sidle over to Atie, glad to see another familiar face. "Hey, any chance you know what this is for? It's kind of messed up that they're making me do this when I'm not even a guard, and also hypothetically sick."
"Oh, we were wondering if any of you are evil. Are you?"
"E-evil's a st-strong word... b-but, not, entirely, uh... off-base... may, be..." Penny squeaks out something that barely qualifies as a clarification.
"Right, yeah, that definitely wasn't what he said."
"What? Evil? No, definitely not. And my friend doesn't have it in him either. Why would they ask that? I mean, would an evil person tell you that they're evil?"
"Who wants to know, anyways? The emperor?"
"Layta'd be one to judge... might as well be the reaper..." Ace mutters.
"Theo, but whatever, that wasn't what he said anyway. He was just asking us for our eyes. I didn't really get it. Oh, and do you know where the emperor is?"
"Uhhh..." I think about it. "Nope. Last time I saw him was with you."
"My liege has other responsibilities." Bixbite interjects. "I was hoping you two would have left by now. Are you planning to stick with us the whole day?"

I startle at how close she suddenly is to us. Was she listening in? Damn it, I need to pay more attention to these things. "Yup, yup. That's true. We'll get out of your hair, ma'am. I'll just be heading back to my room." I give her a smile that I hope seems natural.

Bixbite roughly grabs the back collar of Bucky's shirt. "Not *you*. My liege requested I take you specifically. I meant *those* two." She gestures to Penny and Atie.

Penny sputters out a response. "W-we, um, well... k-keep an eye... we, uh, we're gonna... be with you, yes, that's!!! Yes, we, we are, yes... mhm!"
"Um. Theo left us behind so that Penny could explain a metaphor to me. I don't even know where he is, honestly. Besides, we just got here..."
"Wagh!"
I stumble back a bit, trying not to seem like I'm resisting.

Bixbite rolls her head around, thinking this over. "Right. That's fine. It might be better to have some Newarkers there to witness our victory." She lets go of Bucky, and speaks in a booming voice to the room. "We shall be finishing our journey to Paradise today! This group has been handpicked as the most elite of our empire! For our Emperor, our Princess, and our Hero! We will make history!" The crowd of royal guards cross their arms into a plus shape, the Yondovan salute.
Atie simply stands in awe. It's not clear what they're talking about.
I rub the back of my neck, annoyed. Does she EVER cut her fingernails? Jeez.
"Hoo-rah..."
Ace shakily joins the salute after remembering that he's dressed as a royal guard right now. Bixbite returns the salute before breaking it off, and begins leading the guards out of the train.
Atie follows, wondering where the others are, and when she will finally know what's going on.
I give the salute too, a bit late. Whatever. They're probably not expecting it from me anyways. I follow along, ready for another bum day of waiting for things to actually, properly start.

Penny and Ace follow their respective companions, and the group begins the final stretch of their path to Paradise. The station is being constructed only a short distance away, so the trip is rather short. After a brief period of time, they come over the crest of a sand dune and witness the appearance of the town they've come all this way for.

It's a quaint town; small buildings constructed primarily out of wood. They've clearly been aged and weathered by time, with the assistance of the harsh desert climate. On one end of the town is a large mansion, surrounded by a lush garden. On the other, a stone tower looms over the town.

Bixbite stretches out her arms, letting the arid winds rush over her. Her face betrays something beneath her stoic demeanor, breaking from her composed character. With an expression full of pure ecstasy, she points to the center of town, towards a large structure covered with a tarp.

"Our victory awaits."
((End session))
Bixbite resumes leading the march into town.
Woah...
The others follow.

It's quite the place... I mean, I haven't seen too much outside of my own town. But this is... different, to say the least. Beaten down. It looks like... a metaphor for the struggles of life, almost... the small, simple people, living in their meagre shacks... the more fortunate, looking down on them with disdain... and the one above them all, standing like stone. I'll need to keep an eye out for more symbolism like this going forward.
"Any idea what's under the tarp, Atty?" I whisper.
"Tarp? What do you mean?"
I point at the structure we're heading towards. "That thing. Maybe tarp is the wrong word?"
"Oh... If the guards are so excited about it and saying they'll win something, maybe it's a huge bomb? Or they're racing and it's a finish line. Uh, that's all I can think of."
"Yeah... I guess I hope it's the latter, if those are the two options, haha."

Following Bixbite's lead, the group weaves through the town, and arrives at the covered structure, at which point the guards begin to fan out. There's a crowd of people already at the structure's base. Closest to the structure are two lawmen wearing sheriff and deputy badges, an unfamiliar man and woman, and a woman that Bucky would recognize as Briar McGregor.
There is currently a massive amount of people in the town square.
Oh! Oh!! Ah, she's okay... I knew it, I knew it. But still, seeing it myself... I'm glad. I run up to Briar and give her a smile. "You made it back!"
Alonsa turns to Briar. “These are… friends of yours?”
Briar opens her eyes widely and smiles "I'm so glad you are okay!"
"I should be the one saying that to you! I heard you got carried away by a copper?"
I poke her in the shoulder. "Was it fun, eh? A little adventure?"
A royal guard waves to Briar with a nervous smile, also looking relieved to see her. After a moment she would probably recognize him as Ace, wearing a royal guard outfit for some reason.
She turns to Alonsa and nods "Yes, I traveled with them" she looks back at Bucky and giggles "It was a little fun"
“Are you from Yondova, then?”

Atie sees Bucky go off to meet someone in the crowd, and is left alone, to a point she feels like an intruder. It's not clear what's happening, so it's confusing that Bucky would personally know anyone here. But then again, she never knew why Bucky was with the emperor either, so maybe she's very important somehow.
Alonsa is incredibly confused and lost

The other people present at this reunion seem less eager to join in the icebreaking. Penny, the third woman accompanying the Yondovan guard, stares at the tarp intensely, her whole body shaking. The deputy glances around at the royal guard surrounding the town square in a defensive stance. A man in a large winter coat near Alonsa keeps his hands in his pockets, and stays silent.

The sheriff keeps his eyes locked on the head of the royal guard, as Alonsa would be able to identify. To others, she would be known as Bixbite. An intimidating woman, who emanates strength. She approaches the tarp, grinning with malice.
I really, really hope it's a finish line.
Atie is anxiously waiting, trying to convince herself that the explosion will probably be so strong it will be painless.
Alonsa looks on apprehensively

Bixbite grips the tarp, and roughly flings it off the structure. As it flutters to the ground, the structure beneath is visible to everyone.

A golden statue, glimmering in the morning sun. It depicts a train extending into the sky, coiling over itself like a snake. It's an ostentatious display, demanding attention. It's surprising, then, that it's only the second most striking item under the tarp.

Entangled in the miniature train cars is a corpse, hanging upside down from the gilded tracks. Its flesh has been horribly burnt, leaving its appearance completely blackened and charred. Its smell is as horrible as the sight. The state it's in should render it unrecognizable beyond the shape of the body, but one identifying detail is left in pristine condition.

The corpse is wearing a bird-like mask.
What the fuck...?
"Is that supposed to look like the emperor of Yondova?"
Briar gasps at the sight of the mask but as she processes the details on the body she looks away gagging. Covering her nose.
“A charred corpse… it would have to have been burned, if not alive then after death.”
“That makes investigation a bit easier, I think.”
"Wait, is that not part of the exhibition?"
"Wait, wait, wait, what do you mean *investigation*? We haven't even... checked if he's alive! Oh my god, guys, somebody needs to get him down from there!!"
Without missing a beat, Bixbite motions to the guards, and yells commands. "Cordon off the town! Don't let anyone out!" They move at her command, scattering to restrict the perimeter of Paradise.
I look around, slightly panicking.
“He is definitely dead.”
"How would you know?!"
“I mean…”
"Burns don't fucking... automatically kill you!"
Penny collapses to the ground, crying uncontrollably, and blubbering to herself.
Aghh...
"The smell... Oh my god" Briar murmurs to herself
"Are you really sure this isn't just a statue intended to mean that the train will ruin Yondova or something??"
“The statue has been here for days. I kinda assumed it was you guys who put it up.”
“The corpse just appeared here yesterday.”
“Or. Last night I guess.”
"How would they build a statue that smells like this, Atie...? And why..."

The sheriff looks deeply annoyed at the raucous crowd. "...Regardless whether it's alive or dead, we should get it down. Can any of y'all... confirm it's really him?"

Bixbite shakes her head, still holding a manic grin. "How could we? No one was allowed to see his face, even if it was still intact under that mask."
"I don't know! It'd be insulting and disturbing, but it'd be way better!"
“Okay wait… I think im missing something.”
“Do you guys know who this is?”
“I have no idea.”
"Can't tell from the body, but it's the mask..."
"I've only seen him once, but the emperor of Yondova was wearing that."
“Wait, really?”
"The emperor wore that mask always during my trip here" Briar answers still pinching her nose and looking away
“That exact one? Hm…”
“That’s terrible…”

I try and work out whether keeping this to myself gives me some kind of strategic advantage, but... the whole thought process makes me even more sick to my stomach... and what if he told Bixbite? What if she knows, and if I don't speak up, she'll know that I'm... urgh...
I raise my hand timidly. "Um, sheriff... I met with him a few days ago, and he... he gave me a way of identifying him, if you... I mean, if you let me give it a shot...? Once he's down from there..."
"Maybe he, like... knew that this would happen?"
Somehow...
He hardly seemed suicidal, though...
Or ready to go.
The sheriff nods. "Right, let's get 'im down, then. Deputy, get us a ladder." The deputy scurries off to do that.
Atie has gradually backed away from the statue to avoid the stench. The tattooed girl either has been following her subconsciously while they talk, or is silently understanding of it.
Ace smiles at Bucky. "I knew... I just knew it... If anyone could solve this, it'd be you. This is great."
Alonsa takes a few steps back.
Briar also steps back with everyone

A man approaches from an alleyway behind Briar. Some may recognize or spot him, but before they have the chance to warn her, she feels a hand on her shoulder. A warm voice meets her ear. "My darling sister, is something the matter?" Theo McGregor... Kit's voice questions her.
She turns around and after a couple of seconds of just staring at him. She smiles and jumps to hug him "Kit! I missed you so much, there is a lot going on"
He returns her hug with enthusiasm, shutting his eyes to truly feel the moment. "It's alright, I'm here now. I'll protect you."
"Theo!"
"Th-the... Theo!!! Th-the... body... Euuugghhh..." Penny wails, still on the ground.
"Did you do this, Theo?"
I'm just nervously tapping my foot, waiting for the ladder guy to make his way around the track.
Somehow, I doubt Theo did it.
...if he's even dead, that is. Which, for the record, we don't know.
Alonsa is mostly just glad suspicion moved away from Thromb
"don't ask that, my brother would never do such a thing"
"I mean, he did almost kill the emperor yesterday, so I donno."
Confused she looks at Kit "You what?"

Theo reluctantly releases the embrace, and glares at Atie. "You sully my sister's ears with such rumors. I played no part in this foul crime. The bastard deserves what he got, for leaving my darling sister behind, but I wasn't the one to escort him out of this world."
"Rumors? I just asked you."
The deputy comes running in with a ladder. "I've got the ladder!" Looks like he found a ladder.
"Ah, okay, yeah... just get it into place, there..." I stop myself from biting my fingernails. One nervous tic is enough.
I jog up to him and try to help him position the ladder.
Oh! Alonsa quickly whips out her notepad and makes a sketch of the statue and the body in it
As well as her rough guesses for type of injury and time of death

"Don't say something like that Kit, he was a person just like all of us" she crosses her arms "I was perfectly fine, there was probably a lot in their plate in that moment. I don't blame him for not looking for me"

Theo stares at his sister with a stunned expression, but after a moment, a deeply loving smile rises to his face. "Of course. My darling sister is so forgiving... I'm sorry these fools have troubled you with such hardships, but you remain so... pure. Your heart holds no room for hatred or resentment. I melt at the beauty of your love even for these creatures."
The ladder placement is an overwhelming success. "So, uh, should I just toss it down, or..." The deputy tries to figure out how to get the corpse down.
“Don’t disturb it too much!”
"Be careful!"
The sheriff hands his deputy a rope. "I reckon we can tie this to the darn thing. We'll lower it nice and easy."
"Don't... don't call him a thing..." I mutter.
“I’d just lift it out… or maybe cut the statue…”
"You want 'im to carry the body and climb down the ladder? Don't want another death on our hands." The sheriff dismisses Alonsa.
